officialDocs.label: Access management and developer token sunset
OAuth overview for the Google Ads API

verdict.summary: Developer tokens were sunset on 2026-09-09: access levels now belong to the Google Cloud project that issues your OAuth credentials, Explorer access (2,880 production operations/day) is usually auto-approved, and Basic (15,000/day) follows brand verification within minutes. The slow part is Google's OAuth app verification for the Google Ads scope (Google Ads docs call it restricted, others call it sensitive), plus a manual audit (about 10 business days) if you need Standard's unlimited operations.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Enabling the API grants Test access immediately (test accounts only); Explorer for production accounts is automated 'in most cases'. Creating test accounts and the OAuth client takes most of the time.

timeToProd.assumes: A multi-user agent that reads reports and manages campaigns at Basic access (15,000 ops/day), which needs brand verification plus Google OAuth app verification for the Google Ads scope; Standard access adds a manual audit of about 10 business days.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Google's OAuth app verification for the Google Ads scope (3–5 business days typical for sensitive scopes, often longer), then automated Basic approval; Standard needs a manual Google compliance review.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Access-level timings are sourced; whether the scope goes through sensitive or restricted verification is unclear, so the range is our estimate.

prerequisites.item: A Google Cloud project with the Google Ads API enabled
prerequisites.why: Since 2026-09-09 the project that generates your OAuth credentials sets your API access level; sign-up and upgrades happen on the Google Ads API Overview page.

prerequisites.item: An OAuth consent screen set to External and In production, with verified branding
prerequisites.why: Brand verification is required before applying for Basic or Standard access, and Google's Ads guide says the app must be External and In production.

prerequisites.item: A paid (non-Free-Trial) Cloud billing account in good standing
prerequisites.why: A known issue causes Basic access rejections for projects on the Free Trial or with a suspended or disabled billing account.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Google lists removing billing or using another brand-verified project as alternative workarounds.

prerequisites.item: Google Ads test accounts for development
prerequisites.why: Test access only works against test accounts until Explorer or higher is granted.

prerequisites.item: A tool that meets the Required Minimum Functionality (for Standard)
prerequisites.why: Standard access applicants must comply with RMF and may need to give Google demo sign-in access.

scopeTiers.impact: 15,000 operations/day against test accounts only. Fine for building; useless for real customers.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The Google Ads API uses a single OAuth scope; access tiers, not scopes, change the review path.

scopeTiers.impact: 2,880 production operations/day. No account creation, user management, keyword/reach planning, or billing services. No brand verification needed, but unverified OAuth apps still face Google's user cap and warning screen.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Explorer review is 'automated review and approval in most cases'.

scopeTiers.impact: 15,000 operations/day on production accounts and all services. Needs brand verification (minutes) and, for many users, Google OAuth app verification of the Google Ads scope.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Basic approval itself is automated and typically within minutes; the 1–4 weeks is the OAuth verification estimate.

scopeTiers.impact: Unlimited daily operations (feature rate limits still apply). Manual audit; permissible use is set to ad management, reporting, or keyword research.

steps.title: Create or pick a Cloud project with paid billing
steps.detail: Use a Google Cloud project on a paid billing account (not Free Trial). This project's access level will govern every OAuth credential it issues.

steps.title: Enable the Google Ads API
steps.detail: Open the Google Ads API Overview page and complete sign-up. This grants Test access (15,000 ops/day, test accounts only). The old API Center (ads.google.com/aw/apicenter) no longer processes applications.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The Overview URL redirected us to Google sign-in (HTTP 302) on 2026-10-20.

steps.title: Create a web OAuth client in the same project
steps.detail: Create a Web application OAuth client ID with your redirect URIs in the same project where the API is enabled.

steps.title: Implement multi-user OAuth
steps.detail: Use Google's OAuth 2.0 web flow with scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords, access_type=offline and prompt=consent to get refresh tokens. Send login-customer-id when operating through a manager account. The developer-token header is now ignored and optional.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The ignored, optional header is from a trade-press summary of Google's announcement; the scope string and login-customer-id usage come from long-standing Google Ads API docs, not a page we fetched today.

steps.title: Apply for Explorer access
steps.detail: On the Overview page, expand Upgrade access level and click Apply for access. Review is automated in most cases and grants 2,880 production operations/day.

steps.title: Draft branding, privacy policy and scope justification
steps.detail: Prepare consistent app name, homepage and privacy policy (on a Search Console-verified domain), a per-scope justification for the Google Ads scope, and a script for the unlisted YouTube demo video showing the consent flow.

steps.title: Verify branding and publish the consent screen
steps.detail: In Google Auth Platform set User type External, publish to In production, fill Branding, click Verify Branding, then Publish branding.

steps.title: Submit OAuth app verification for the Google Ads scope
steps.detail: Add the Google Ads scope to Data Access, record and upload the demo video, and submit for verification.

steps.title: Wait for OAuth verification
steps.detail: Sensitive scope verification typically takes 3–5 business days; Google's Ads docs say the scope is restricted, which (if enforced as such) adds a longer review.

steps.title: Apply for Basic access
steps.detail: With branding verified, return to the Overview page and click Apply for access to move from Explorer to Basic. Approval is automated, typically within minutes.

steps.title: Apply for Standard access if you need volume
steps.detail: From Basic, click Start application. Expect a manual audit (about 10 business days), questions about functionality and audience, RMF compliance and demo sign-in access; reply to Google Compliance emails promptly.

agentCanDo: Implement the multi-user OAuth flow with offline refresh tokens
Draft the privacy policy, scope justification and demo-video script
Track daily operation counts against the access-level cap
Check RMF compliance before a Standard application
humanMustDo: Set up a Cloud project on paid billing and enable the API
Verify the domain in Search Console and verify branding
Record the demo video and submit OAuth verification
Click Apply for Explorer, Basic and Standard access
Answer Google Compliance emails during the Standard audit

blockers.symptom: Basic application rejected: "Basic Access requires a successfully verified OAuth brand profile."
blockers.cause: Brand verification isn't complete, or (known issue) the project is on the Free Trial or has a suspended or disabled billing account.
blockers.fix: Complete brand verification with an External, In-production app; upgrade billing to a paid tier or use a different brand-verified project.

blockers.symptom: Pending Basic application from the API Center disappeared or was closed
blockers.cause: Applications submitted through the API Center before 2026-09-09 were closed when developer tokens were sunset.
blockers.fix: Re-apply from the Google Ads API Overview page in Cloud Console.

blockers.symptom: Calls to production accounts fail while test accounts work
blockers.cause: The project only has Test access.
blockers.fix: Apply for Explorer access on the Overview page.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error string wasn't checked.

blockers.symptom: Account creation, user management, keyword planning or billing calls are refused at Explorer
Requests start failing late in the day with quota errors
blockers.cause: The project exceeded its daily operations cap (2,880 Explorer, 15,000 Basic) over a sliding 24-hour window, shared across all your users.
blockers.fix: Use SearchStream and batch mutates to cut operations, cache reports, or apply for Standard.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Caps and sliding window are sourced; that one project-level cap covers all users is our reading of project-based access.

blockers.symptom: Users see Google's unverified-app warning, or new users are blocked
blockers.cause: The OAuth app hasn't passed verification for the Google Ads scope; unverified apps are user-capped.
blockers.fix: Complete OAuth app verification before launching to customers.

nuances.text: A Google Ads manager account is no longer required to use the API; it's only needed to link and manage multiple accounts through the API.

Existing integrations keep working after the token sunset: access levels were mapped to Cloud projects from recent API activity, and the developer-token header is optional and ignored. Google plans to reject developer tokens in a future major API version, so remove the header.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From a trade-press summary of Google's announcement; Google's deprecations page confirms the sunset only.

nuances.text: Older usage-based restrictions carry over: projects that hadn't used Customer Match (Oct 2025–Mar 2026) or offline conversion uploads (Dec 2025–Jun 2026) are restricted from them and pointed to the Data Manager API.
Standard access is tied to a permissible use (ad management, reporting-only, or keyword research); a reporting-only agent that later wants to mutate campaigns must file a permissible-use change.
In Testing publishing status, external users' refresh tokens expire after 7 days for non-basic scopes; publish to production (which brand verification requires anyway) to avoid this.
Google's Ads docs call the Google Ads OAuth scope 'restricted', while other guides call it sensitive; plan for verification either way before onboarding customers.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Conflicting classifications; we couldn't confirm which review path Google applies.
